newsitem.title: INDIA: Petroleum price hike fears drag down Delhi shares.
newsitem.headline: Petroleum price hike fears drag down Delhi shares.

text.p: Delhi shares opened lower in subdued trade on Wednesday, weighed down by speculation that the government planned to raise petroleum product prices, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's sensitive index dropped 9.30 points to 756.62 after the first 30 minutes of trade.
Indian Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral says the government plans to take a bold decision on cutting losses due to a subsidy the state pays oil firms to sell petroleum products cheaply.
"Despite a persistent fall in stock prices, financial institutions were on the sidelines in early trading, which further affected the markets," said Shree Bhagwan of brokers Means Leasing.
TISCO fell 1.95 rupees to 171.30 on selling by financial institutions.
